title: make localhost HTTPS easy for local testing
problem_statement: Local HTTPS is documented but requires manual TLS env vars; user wants to use localhost over HTTPS.
validated_decisions: `serve.sh` already has HTTP and HTTPS modes.
`https_server.py` is tracked but points to `cert.pem`, which is not the current local cert naming.
draft_assumptions_in_play: Local self-signed certificates are acceptable for development.
Runtime game files must not change.
The generated cert/key must remain untracked.
current_direction: Make `./serve.sh --https` work with default local cert paths.
Generate a self-signed localhost certificate automatically when missing and `openssl` is available.
Keep HTTPS serving dependency-free beyond Python and OpenSSL.
Align `https_server.py` with the same local certificate files.
explicit_non_goals: No dependency manager or package.json introduction.
No committed TLS private key or certificate.
backward_compatibility_concerns: Existing HTTP mode must keep working.
Existing explicit TLS_CERT/TLS_KEY usage must keep working.
required_validations: Start HTTPS server locally and verify an HTTPS response.
JSON parse for thread state/log files.
human_test_checklist: Accept the self-signed certificate warning if the browser prompts.
solution_applied: `./serve.sh --https` now serves HTTPS localhost with default local cert files.
Default local certificates are generated or refreshed when missing SAN for localhost.
`https_server.py` now uses the same local certificate defaults and supports `HOST`/`PORT` overrides.
README documents the one-command HTTPS workflow.
decision_log_summary: Task-orchestrator approved direct build because scope is local tooling only, with no gameplay files touched.
Build-agent implemented local HTTPS tooling and validations.
Review-maintainability-guard returned APPROVE_WITH_NOTES; browser self-signed warning remains expected manual step.
